newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish LOT airline's domestic unit starts service.
newsitem.headline: Polish LOT airline's domestic unit starts service.

text.p: EuroLOT SA, a domestic carrier 100 percent owned by Polish airline Polskie Linie Lotnicze LOT SA, (LOT) on Wednesday began passenger services on routes within Poland.
LOT President Jan Litwinski told a news conference that the two lines would cooperate and not compete with each other.
"LOT and EuroLOT are not competitors on the market, they serve different segments and cooperate on the level of trade and operations," he said.

EuroLOT said in a statement it has leased from its parent company eight ATR-72, which will make initially 200 flights a week connecting six major Polish cities: Warsaw, Gdansk, Krakow, Poznan, Wroclaw and Szczecin.
Marek Rymkiewicz, EuroLOT president, also present, said that the company planned to buy 2-5 aircraft seating 30-40 passengers to boost the number of domestic flights.
He added that domestic connections had been losing money but economic expansion, an increase in business travel and investments in airports should help the company break even in 2000 or 2001.
Rymkiewicz also said that EuroLOT planned to start operating short-range international flights to such cities as Tallin, Riga, Vilnius, Lvov, Vienna and Copenhagen.
